items.title: 2024 Water Efficiency Excellence Award
notes:
Regional Council recognized the Carlsberg Canada (formerly known as Waterloo Brewing) as this year’s Water Efficiency Excellence Award recipient and presented the award to Derek Cairney, Utilities Specialist.

This annual award is given to a business, institution, or organization that takes the initiative to research water savings programs and makes an investment to implement a solution that achieves significant water savings.

In 2023, Carlsberg Canada was the fourth highest water user in the Region of Waterloo and in the same year reduced their water use by 100,000 cubic meters, the equivalent water use of over 1800 people or 450 homes in a year. The project qualified for $10,000 in funding through the Region’s Water Efficient Technology (WET) program to help with the $32,000 total cost of the work.

items.title: Taylor Bulstrode and Amie Sider, Kinbridge Community Association
notes: T. Bulstrode and A. Sider provided a presentation on the positive impact of the YouthForce program.  A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. The community-lead program works in collaboration with Waterloo Regional Housing. The presentation included experiences of several individuals that have benefited from the program. They highlighted that the program helps to provide training, certifications, and wraparound support for equity deserving youth. Also, the program focuses on housing quality, tenant engagement, and community pride. They noted the ongoing successes of their relationship with the Region of Waterloo and requested the continued annual financial support of $100,000 in the 2026 budget.

items.title: Board of Health Update
notes:
Council recognized the remarkable accomplishments of Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, whose contributions continue to shape the future of public health in Ontario. Dr. H. Wang was recently honored with the Association of Local Public Health Agencies of Ontario (alPHa) Distinguished Service Award in recognition of her outstanding contributions to public health in Ontario. She has held numerous influential positions, including serving as the Chair of the Council of Medical Officers of Health and the Vice-Chair of the Board.

Dr. H Wang provided a Board of Health updated. She highlighted that the province-wide measles outbreak has ended, annual enforcement of the Immunization of School Pupils Act, and the Region's preparations for the Fall and Winter respiratory seasons. She also provided a reminder to get vacancies when feasible.

In response to Council, Dr. H. Wang explained that the Region and Public Health do not have jurisdiction over the medical doctor shortage, however, staff can look into what information is available related to this matter.

notes:
Responding to Council, D. Spooner confirmed that staff have been investigating communication options to ensure that Grand River Transit (GRT) customers are aware of the mobility device securement program and ensure that transit operators are ready to assist when requested. 

In response to Council, Rod Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development & Legislative Services, confirmed that the Ministry circulated notice related to the Brownfields Community Improvement Plan (BCIP), which is a joint tax increment grant provided by the Region of Waterloo and the City of Waterloo. The notice stated that the Ministry is working toward a solution to allow for the continuation of the joint grant. He confirmed that Staff are evaluating the Ministry's letter and will be providing further information to Council with potential options.

C. James expressed concern about the increase in hate being experienced throughout the Region and the impact of this hate forcing community events to be cancelled due to threats and potential harm. K. Redman agreed and highlighted that the Regional Anti-Campaign is being launched on October 23, 2025.

J. Liggett highlighted various community events being held in the City of Cambridge such as Handmaiden Tales tours.

J. Gowing reminded Council and the community that the Legion's poppy campaign will begin on October 31, 2025 and encouraged that members of the public attend Remembrance Day Ceremonies on November 11th. B. Vrbanovic provided a further reminder the Sikh Remembrance Day is an annual ceremony held in Kitchener, Ontario, to honour the contributions of Sikh soldiers in the world wars. Canada Post also unveiled a new commemorative stamp honouring Sikh Canadian soldiers during the ceremony.

motions.item_title: Administration and Finance Committee Summary - October 7, 2025
motions.text: The Administration and Finance Committee recommends as follows: WHEREAS The Region of Waterloo is in the midst of enacting an automated speed enforcement plan rooted in changing driver behaviour, increasing public safety, and saving lives following a pilot program that began in 2021; WHEREAS Ontario’s Premier Doug Ford publicly announced the intention to ban automated speed enforcement province-wide in forthcoming legislation; WHEREAS details remain limited of such a bill or legislation and next steps for municipal operators of automated speed enforcement are unclear; WHEREAS The Region of Waterloo has invested significantly in automated speed enforcement, with a program committed to expanding speed cameras to all eligible schools across Waterloo Region by 2028, and is heading into budget deliberations for 2026; WHEREAS automated speed enforcement cameras generate an 87% drop in number of vehicles driving more than 20km/h over the speed limit (source: SickKids/TMU study, July 2025 and that in Waterloo Region, the 85th percentile speed has decreased by over 16km/h on average in school zones covered by a speed camera. THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT The Region of Waterloo halt any further previously planned expansion, AT 28 SCHOOL ZONES, of the automated speed enforcement program until details of the pending legislation are made available. The Region of Waterloo halt any further hiring of staff to deliver on the automated speed enforcement program and that; The Region of Waterloo maintain operation of the current automated speed enforcement program as-is today to provide clarity for drivers, community members, pedestrians, and staff and that; Regional Council requests Region of Waterloo staff report back to Council on the implications of ending the automated speed enforcement program in the Region of Waterloo pending forthcoming Provincial legislation. The Region of Waterloo halt any further previously planned expansion, AT 28 SCHOOL ZONES, of the automated speed enforcement program until details of the pending legislation are made available.
motions.text_html:
The Administration and Finance Committee recommends as follows:

  1. WHEREAS The Region of Waterloo is in the midst of enacting an automated speed enforcement plan rooted in changing driver behaviour, increasing public safety, and saving lives following a pilot program that began in 2021;
    WHEREAS Ontario’s Premier Doug Ford publicly announced the intention to ban automated speed enforcement province-wide in forthcoming legislation;
    WHEREAS details remain limited of such a bill or legislation and next steps for municipal operators of automated speed enforcement are unclear;
    WHEREAS The Region of Waterloo has invested significantly in automated speed enforcement, with a program committed to expanding speed cameras to all eligible schools across Waterloo Region by 2028, and is heading into budget deliberations for 2026;
    WHEREAS automated speed enforcement cameras generate an 87% drop in number of vehicles driving more than 20km/h over the speed limit (source: SickKids/TMU study, July 2025 and that in Waterloo Region, the 85th percentile speed has decreased by over 16km/h on average in school zones covered by a speed camera.
    THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT
    The Region of Waterloo halt any further previously planned expansion, AT 28 SCHOOL ZONES, of the automated speed enforcement program until details of the pending legislation are made available.
    The Region of Waterloo halt any further hiring of staff to deliver on the automated speed enforcement program and that;
    The Region of Waterloo maintain operation of the current automated speed enforcement program as-is today to provide clarity for drivers, community members, pedestrians, and staff and that;
    Regional Council requests Region of Waterloo staff report back to Council on the implications of ending the automated speed enforcement program in the Region of Waterloo pending forthcoming Provincial legislation.
    The Region of Waterloo halt any further previously planned expansion, AT 28 SCHOOL ZONES, of the automated speed enforcement program until details of the pending legislation are made available.

motions.item_title: Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee Summary - October 7, 2025
motions.text: The Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee recommends as follows: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo support the draft water quantity policy amendments related to the Guelph and Guelph/Eramosa Township (G-GET) Quantity Wellhead Protection Area (WHPA-Q) that apply within the Region of Waterloo in the draft amended Grand River Source Protection Plan, as described in Report EES-WIM-25-002, dated October 7, 2025. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the expropriation of lands for Road Improvements to Erb Street West (Regional Road 9) between Ira Needles Boulevard and Gate 1 at the Waste Management Facility, in the City of Waterloo, in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, as detailed in Report PDL-LEG-25-034, dated October 7, 2025, described as follows: Fee Simple Partial Taking: Part of Lot 41, German Company Tract, being Parts 19 and 22 on 58R-21533, City of Waterloo, part of PIN 22684-3604 (LT), (658 Erb Street West, Waterloo) Temporary Easement – Grading: The right and easement, being a temporary easement in gross, for the free and unobstructed, right, interest and easement terminating on the 31st day of December, 2028, for itself, its successors and assigns, and anyone authorized by it, on, over, under and through the following properties for the purposes of excavation, construction, installation, replacement, alteration, grading, and landscaping as required in connection with the construction of a roundabout at Erb Street West (Regional Road 9) and Bourdeaux Place, City of Waterloo, and all related improvements, and works ancillary thereto and for such purposes, the free, unimpeded and unobstructed access to the lands at all times by employees, agents, contractors, workers and anyone authorized by it, and vehicles, supplies and equipment at all times and for all purposes and things necessary for or incidental to the exercise and enjoyment of the right and easement: Part of Lot 41, German Company Tract, being Parts 20, 21 and 23 on 58R-21533, City of Waterloo, part of PIN 22684-3604 (LT), (658 Erb Street West, Waterloo) And that staff be instructed to register a Plan of Expropriation for the properties within three months of the granting of the approval to expropriate the properties, as required by the Expropriations Act; And that the registered owners be served with a Notice of Expropriation, Notice of Election and a Notice of Possession for the properties after the registration of the Plan of Expropriation and the Regional Solicitor is authorized to take any and all actions required to enforce such Notices including but not limited to any application pursuant to Section 40 of the Expropriations Act; And that the Regional Solicitor is authorized to enter into an agreement with the registered owners, or to make an application under Section 39 of the Expropriations Act, to adjust the date for possession specified in the Notice of Possession as may be required; And that all above-referenced fee simple partial takings situated adjacent to an existing Regional public highway be acquired for road widening purposes and therefore be deemed to form part of the adjacent public highway in accordance with subsection 31(6) of the Municipal Act, 2001; And that if no agreement as to compensation is made with an owner, the statutory Offer of Compensation and payment be served upon the registered owners of the properties in the amount of the market value of the interests in the land as estimated by the Region’s appraiser in accordance with the Expropriations Act; And that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to execute any Indemnity agreement or other document related to payment of the statutory Offer of Compensation; And further that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to discontinue expropriation proceedings or any part thereof, in respect of the above described lands, or any part thereof, upon the registration on title of the required documentation to complete the transaction or if determined by the Commissioner, Engineering & Environmental Services, that such lands, or any part or interest thereof, are not required for the subject Project. 4. Whereas under Ontario Regulation 391/2, Blue Box producers are fully accountable and financially responsible for their products and packaging once they reach their end of life and are disposed of for ‘eligible’ sources only; and Whereas ‘ineligible’ sources, which producers are not responsible for, include business improvement areas, places of worship, daycares, camp grounds, public facing and internal areas of municipal-owned buildings, and not-for-profit organizations, such as shelters and food banks; and Whereas the province amended Ontario Regulation 391/2 to not expand services for new public space recycling; and Whereas should a municipality continue to provide services to the ‘ineligible’ sources, the municipality will be required to oversee the collection, transportation, and processing of the recycling, assuming 100% of the costs; and Therefore, be it resolved that Region of Waterloo Council request that the province amend Ontario Regulation 391/21, Blue Box so that producers are responsible for the end-of-life management of recycling products from all sources as stated above; and Further that Council request the support of all Ontario Municipalities; and THAT this resolution be forwarded to the Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, the Honourable Todd McCarthy, Minister of the Environment, Conservation, and Parks, Mike Harris, Minister of Natural Resources and Forestry, Minister of Affairs and Housing, Rob Flack, AMO President Robin Jones, Waterloo Region municipalities, all Ontario Municipalities and First Nation Councils. That Minister McCarthy be asked to provide more information on the estimated $171M in savings for municipalities through this program.

The Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee recommends as follows:

  1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo support the draft water quantity policy amendments related to the Guelph and Guelph/Eramosa Township (G-GET) Quantity Wellhead Protection Area (WHPA-Q) that apply within the Region of Waterloo in the draft amended Grand River Source Protection Plan, as described in Report EES-WIM-25-002, dated October 7, 2025.
  2. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the expropriation of lands for Road Improvements to Erb Street West (Regional Road 9) between Ira Needles Boulevard and Gate 1 at the Waste Management Facility, in the City of Waterloo, in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, as detailed in Report PDL-LEG-25-034, dated October 7, 2025, described as follows:
    Fee Simple Partial Taking:
    1. Part of Lot 41, German Company Tract, being Parts 19 and 22 on 58R-21533, City of Waterloo, part of PIN 22684-3604 (LT), (658 Erb Street West, Waterloo)

Temporary Easement – Grading:
The right and easement, being a temporary easement in gross, for the free and unobstructed, right, interest and easement terminating on the 31st day of December, 2028, for itself, its successors and assigns, and anyone authorized by it, on, over, under and through the following properties for the purposes of excavation, construction, installation, replacement, alteration, grading, and landscaping as required in connection with the construction of a roundabout at Erb Street West (Regional Road 9) and Bourdeaux Place, City of Waterloo, and all related improvements, and works ancillary thereto and for such purposes, the free, unimpeded and unobstructed access to the lands at all times by employees, agents, contractors, workers and anyone authorized by it, and vehicles, supplies and equipment at all times and for all purposes and things necessary for or incidental to the exercise and enjoyment of the right and easement:

    1. Part of Lot 41, German Company Tract, being Parts 20, 21 and 23 on 58R-21533, City of Waterloo, part of PIN 22684-3604 (LT), (658 Erb Street West, Waterloo)

And that staff be instructed to register a Plan of Expropriation for the properties within three months of the granting of the approval to expropriate the properties, as required by the Expropriations Act;
And that the registered owners be served with a Notice of Expropriation, Notice of Election and a Notice of Possession for the properties after the registration of the Plan of Expropriation and the Regional Solicitor is authorized to take any and all actions required to enforce such Notices including but not limited to any application pursuant to Section 40 of the Expropriations Act;
And that the Regional Solicitor is authorized to enter into an agreement with the registered owners, or to make an application under Section 39 of the Expropriations Act, to adjust the date for possession specified in the Notice of Possession as may be required;
And that all above-referenced fee simple partial takings situated adjacent to an existing Regional public highway be acquired for road widening purposes and therefore be deemed to form part of the adjacent public highway in accordance with subsection 31(6) of the Municipal Act, 2001;
And that if no agreement as to compensation is made with an owner, the statutory Offer of Compensation and payment be served upon the registered owners of the properties in the amount of the market value of the interests in the land as estimated by the Region’s appraiser in accordance with the Expropriations Act;
And that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to execute any Indemnity agreement or other document related to payment of the statutory Offer of Compensation;
And further that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to discontinue expropriation proceedings or any part thereof, in respect of the above described lands, or any part thereof, upon the registration on title of the required documentation to complete the transaction or if determined by the Commissioner, Engineering & Environmental Services, that such lands, or any part or interest thereof, are not required for the subject Project.

4. Whereas under Ontario Regulation 391/2, Blue Box producers are fully accountable and financially responsible for their products and packaging once they reach their end of life and are disposed of for ‘eligible’ sources only; and
Whereas ‘ineligible’ sources, which producers are not responsible for, include business improvement areas, places of worship, daycares, camp grounds, public facing and internal areas of municipal-owned buildings, and not-for-profit  organizations, such as shelters and food banks; and
Whereas the province amended Ontario Regulation 391/2 to not expand services for new public space recycling; and
Whereas should a municipality continue to provide services to the ‘ineligible’ sources, the municipality will be required to oversee the collection, transportation, and processing of the recycling, assuming 100% of the costs; and
Therefore, be it resolved that Region of Waterloo Council request that the province amend Ontario Regulation 391/21, Blue Box so that producers are responsible for the end-of-life management of recycling products from all sources as stated above; and
Further that Council request the support of all Ontario Municipalities; and
THAT this resolution be forwarded to the Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, the Honourable Todd McCarthy, Minister of the Environment, Conservation, and Parks, Mike Harris, Minister of Natural Resources and Forestry, Minister of Affairs and Housing, Rob Flack, AMO President Robin Jones, Waterloo Region municipalities, all Ontario Municipalities and First Nation Councils.
That Minister McCarthy be asked to provide more information on the estimated $171M in savings for municipalities through this program.
